paper.title_en: Emergence and polymer physics of the center-vortex network: Confronting SU(4) lattice Yang-Mills theory
paper.abstract_en: The geometric organization and statistical properties of center-vortex networks provide a window into the infrared dynamics underlying confinement in Yang-Mills theory. Motivated by this connection, we investigate new consequences of a previously proposed confinement mechanism based on physically equivalent elementary Cartan fluxes. We show that, in the percolating phase, these fluxes dynamically reorganize into center-charge sectors whose dominant vortex tensions satisfy a Casimir scaling law, similar to that observed for confining string tensions. We then confront this result with the first nontrivial Yang-Mills case: the doubly charged vortex chains recently observed in SU(4) lattice simulations. To extract the parameters needed to connect the lattice ensemble with the effective description, we characterize how center-vortex chains grow and bend in SU(3) and SU(4) using polymer-inspired techniques not previously applied to center vortices. We find good quantitative agreement for the SU(4) doubly charged sector, providing further evidence for the proposed mechanism.
